professional [[basketball]] player for [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Nicknamed the "'''Latvian Laser'''",{{cite web |title=Wizards Featured: Davis Bertans |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-featured-davis-bertans-latvian-laser |access-date=26 April 2021 |website=NBA.com|type=video}} he also represents the [[Latvia men's national basketball team|Latvian national team]]. He was the 42nd pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]]. ==Professional career== ===Kadeti (2007–2008)=== In 2007–08, Bertāns played for ASK Kadeti II. ===Riga (2008–2010)=== Between 2008 and 2010, Bertāns played for BAA Riga of Latvia's second division. During this time, he also had two stints in the top division with [[ASK Riga]] at the end of the 2008–09 season, and with BK Keizarmezs Riga at the start of the 2009–10 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft/2011/prospects/davis-bertans/|title=Prospect Profile: Davis Bertans|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=27 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915152247/http://www.nba.com/draft/2011/prospects/davis-bertans/|archive-date=15 September 2017|url-status=dead}} ===Barons (2010)=== Bertāns started the 2010–11 season with [[BK Barons]]. ===Olimpija (2010–2012)=== In November 2010, Bertāns signed a multi-year deal with Slovenian club [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija]].{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/78447/union-olimpija-signs-top-prospect-bertans | title=Union Olimpija signs top prospect Bertans | work=Euroleague.net | date=14 November 2010 | access-date=14 July 2016}} Following the 2010–11 season, Bertāns was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 42nd overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. However, his rights were immediately traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] along with the rights to 15th overall pick [[Kawhi Leonard]] for [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-obtain-draft-rights-kawhi-leonard|title=Spurs Obtain Draft Rights To Kawhi Leonard|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=23 June 2011|access-date=4 January 2012}} ===Partizan (2012–2014)=== In January 2012, Bertāns left Olimpija and signed a three-and-a-half-year contract with Serbian club [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]].{{cite news | url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/89619/partizan-belgrade-lands-davis-bertans.html | title=Partizan Belgrade lands Davis Bertans | work=Sportando.com | date=4 January 2012 | access-date=14 July 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820154427/http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/89619/partizan-belgrade-lands-davis-bertans.html | archive-date=20 August 2016 | url-status=dead }} In the Serbian League finals series against [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] in June 2013, he tore the [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in his right knee, which sidelined him for nine months.{{cite web|title=Bertans pokidao ligamente kolena!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2013&mm=06&dd=13&nav_id=722651|work=b92.net|date=13 June 2013|access-date=14 March 2014|language=sr}}{{cite web|title=Partizan's Davis Bertans won't return before March|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/107300/partizan-s-davis-bertans-won-t-return-before-march.html|work=Sportando.com|date=24 October 2013|access-date=14 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709234054/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/107300/partizan-s-davis-bertans-won-t-return-before-march.html|archive-date=9 July 2017|url-status=dead}} Bertāns returned to the court on 20 March 2014, against [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], helping his team get a hard-fought [[Euroleague 2013–14 Top 16 Group F|Euroleague Top 16]] win against the favoured visitors by contributing two points, two rebounds and one assist in 15 minutes of action.{{cite web|title=Partizan rallies to beat Maccabi in closing seconds|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=207&pcode=002821&seasoncode=E2013#!report|work=Euroleague.net|date=20 March 2014|access-date=21 March 2014}} Eight days later, on 28 March 2014, Dāvis scored team-high 20 points in a road Euroleague Top 16 loss to [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv-Kuban]].{{cite web|title=Brown, Likhodey lead Lokomotiv to key home win|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=214&pcode=003458&seasoncode=E2013#!report|work=Euroleague.net|date=28 March 2014|access-date=28 March 2014}} Partizan ended the season by winning its 13th and Dāvis' third consecutive [[2013–14 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] title, defeating rivals Crvena zvezda 3–1 in the finals series.{{cite web|title=Ništa novo, Partizan je šampion!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=06&dd=21&nav_id=865626|work=b92.net|date=21 June 2014|access-date=21 June 2014|language=sr}} On 3 July 2014, Bertāns terminated his contract with the club.{{cite web|title=Agent: Bertans raskinuo ugovor|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=07&dd=03&nav_id=871782|work=b92.net|date=3 July 2014|access-date=3 July 2014|language=sr}} ===Baskonia (2014–2016)=== On 19 July 2014, Bertāns signed a three-year contract with Spanish club [[Laboral Kutxa Baskonia]].{{cite web|title=Labor [sic] Kutxa signs up Latvian forward Davis Bertans|url=http://www.baskonia.com/en/laboral-kutxa-incorpora-al-alero-leton-davis-bertans-2/|work=Baskonia.com|date=19 July 2014|access-date=19 July 2014}}{{cite web|title=Laboral Kutxa Vitoria adds shooter Bertans|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138667/laboral-kutxa-vitoria-adds-shooter-bertans|work=Euroleague.net|date=19 July 2014|access-date=19 July 2014}} On 26 March 2015, in a game against [[Emporio Armani Milano]], Bertāns tore the [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in his right knee, the same injury that sidelined him in 2013.{{cite web|title=Laboral's Bertans to miss rest of the season|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5uhhxosqa5jv9nxl/laboral-s-bertans-to-miss-rest-of-the-season|work=Euroleague.net|date=27 March 2015|access-date=27 March 2015}} He was subsequently ruled out for six to eight months.{{cite news|title=Bertans definitivno pokidao ACL|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=03&dd=27&nav_id=973528|work=b92.net|date=27 March 2015|access-date=27 March 2015|language=sr}} Over 22 [[2014–15 Euroleague|Euroleague]] games, he averaged 11.0 points and 2.9 rebounds per game, while also averaging 11.4 points in 25 games of the [[2014–15 ACB season|Spanish League]]. In Laboral Kutxa Baskonia's very next game following Bertāns's injury, a Spanish League contest versus [[Valencia BC]], each Baskonia player wore Bertāns's number 42 in a show of support for their sidelined teammate.{{cite news|title=Dirljiv gest saigrača za Bertansa|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=03&dd=29&nav_id=974230|work=b92.net|date=29 March 2015|access-date=29 March 2015|language=sr}} On 14 July 2016, Bertāns and Baskonia agreed on a contract buyout.{{cite web|url=http://www.baskonia.com/en/davis-bertans-saski-baskonia-agree-on-contract-buyout/|title=Davis Bertans, Saski baskonia [sic] agree on contract buyout|work=Baskonia.com|date=14 July 2016|access-date=14 July 2016}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2016–2019)=== On 14 July 2016, Bertāns signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/san-antonio-signs-davis-bertans|title=SAN ANTONIO SIGNS DAVIS BERTANS|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=14 July 2016|access-date=14 July 2016}} He made his debut for the Spurs in their season-opener on 25 October 2016, scoring five points in four minutes off the bench in a 129–100 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899377|title=Spurs vs. Warriors – Box Score|publisher=ESPN|date=25 October 2016|access-date=29 October 2016}} On 25 November 2016, he set a career high in scoring, pitching in 15 of the Spurs' 56 bench points to help San Antonio defeat the [[Boston Celtics]] 109–103.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899675|title=Spurs top Boston 109–103 on Leonard's 25 points, 10 rebounds|publisher=ESPN|date=25 November 2016|access-date=26 November 2016}} On 7 January 2017, he scored 21 points in a 102–85 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. He went 4-of-5 on three-pointers in leading the Spurs in scoring for the first time in 2016–17.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899979|title=Rookie Bertans' 21 points lead Spurs over Hornets, 102–85|publisher=ESPN|date=7 January 2017|access-date=7 January 2017}} On 29 January 2017, against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], Bertāns became just the fourth Spurs rookie with at least 35 three-pointers and 15 blocks in a season, joining [[Kawhi Leonard]], [[Manu Ginóbili]] and [[Lloyd Daniels]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900138|title=Curry's 24 points help Mavericks hold off Spurs, 105–101|publisher=ESPN|date=29 January 2017|access-date=30 January 2017}} On 11 March 2017, he had three three-pointers in a 107–85 win over Golden State to reach 51 three-pointers on the season. He became just the sixth Spurs rookie to hit 50 in a season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900375|title=Mills leads Spurs past Warriors in game minus top stars|publisher=ESPN|date=11 March 2017|access-date=12 March 2017}} During his rookie season, he had multiple [[NBA G League|assignments]] with the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=8 January 2018}} Early on the 2017–18 season, Bertāns was twice assigned to the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2017–18 NBA Assignments|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=8 January 2018}} On 8 January 2018, he scored a career-high 28 points on 11-of-15 shooting with six 3-pointers in a 107–100 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975342|title=Aldridge, Bertans lead Spurs to comeback win over Kings|publisher=ESPN|date=8 January 2018|access-date=8 January 2018}} On 13 January 2018, he scored 18 points on a career-high six 3-pointers in a 112–80 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975379|title=Leonard, Bertans lead Spurs to 112–80 win over Denver|publisher=ESPN|date=13 January 2018|access-date=14 January 2018}} On 11 July 2018, Bertāns re-signed with the Spurs for two years and $14 million.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-re-sign-davis-bertans|title=SPURS RE-SIGN DAVIS BERTANS|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=11 July 2018|access-date=11 July 2018}} On 27 January 2019, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 132–119 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071414|title=Aldridge leads Spurs past Wizards 132–119|publisher=ESPN|date=27 January 2019|access-date=27 January 2019}} ===Washington Wizards (2019–2022)=== On 6 July 2019, Bertāns was traded from the [[San Antonio Spurs]] to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a three-team deal that also included the [[Brooklyn Nets]], in which the Spurs received [[DeMarre Carroll]] via sign-and-trade.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-davis-bertans-from-spurs-aaron-white|title=Wizards acquire Davis Bertans from Spurs|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=6 July 2019}} In his first game against San Antonio following the trade, on 26 October 2019, Bertāns made all seven of his field goal attempts, including five three-pointers, and scored 23 points.{{cite web|last=Garcia|first=Jeff|url=https://news4sanantonio.com/sports/spurs-zone/davis-bertans-overcome-with-emotion-in-return-to-san-Antonio|title=Davis Bertans overcome with emotion in return to San Antonio|publisher=WOAI-TV|date=28 October 2019|access-date=3 December 2019}} On 22 November, he made six three-pointers and scored 20 points against the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|last=DePrisco|first=Mike|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/tying-career-high-threes-game-davis-bertans-has-yet-find-three-too-deep-him|title=Tying a career-high for threes in a game, Davis Bertans has yet to find a three too deep for him|website=NBC Sports Washington|date=22 November 2019|access-date=3 December 2019}} On 22 June 2020, three months into the NBA's hiatus, Bertāns decided to pull out of the NBA's [[2020 NBA Bubble|Orlando restart]]; he was the first player to do so. This decision was made for personal reasons.{{cite web | last=Terranova | first=Justin | title=Davis Bertans is first NBA player to pull out of restart | website=New York Post | date=2020-06-22 | url=https://nypost.com/2020/06/22/wizards-davis-bertans-decides-to-sit-out-nbas-restart/ | access-date=2025-12-14}} Bertāns was entering free agency and viewed sitting out as a preventative measure. Bertāns also had two previous ACL injuries. If the Wizards did not advance past the seeding games in Orlando, he stood to lose $520,000. The Washington Wizards fully supported Bertāns's decision and as anticipated did not ultimately qualify for the playoffs. On 21 November 2020, Bertāns agreed to a five-year, $80 million deal with the Washington Wizards.{{Cite web|date=21 November 2020|title=Bertans sticks with Wizards on 5-year, $80M deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30355964/washington-wizards-davis-bertans-agree-5-year-80-million-deal|access-date=21 November 2020|publisher=ESPN|language=en}} On 17 February 2021, Bertāns scored a career-high 35 points in a 130–128 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He logged a career-best nine 3-pointers becoming the third player in team history to do so.{{Cite web|title=Recap: Bertans scores career-high 35, leads Wizards in 130–128 win over Nuggets|url=https://www.nba.com/amp/wizards/wizards-nuggets-recap-021721|access-date=19 February 2021|publisher=National Basketball Association}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2022–2023)=== On 10 February 2022, Bertāns, along with [[Spencer Dinwiddie]], was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Kristaps Porziņģis]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavstradeporzingis/|publisher=National Basketball Association|title=Mavs trade Porzingis to Wizards for Dinwiddie and Bertans|date=10 February 2022|access-date=10 February 2022}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2023–2024)=== On 6 July 2023, Bertāns, along with the 10th pick of the [[2023 NBA draft]], was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for the 12th pick of the draft.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-wallace-bertans-230706|title=Thunder Acquires Cason Wallace and Dāvis Bertāns|website=nba.com|date=July 6, 2023}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2024)=== On 8 February 2024, Bertāns was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]], along with [[Tre Mann]], [[Vasilije Micić]], a 2024 second-round pick, a 2025 second-round pick and cash considerations, in exchange for [[Gordon Hayward]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Davis Bertans, Tre Mann, Vasilije Micic And Two Second-Round Picks From Oklahoma City|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-davis-bertans-tre-mann-vasilije-micic-and-two-second-round-picks-from-oklahoma-city|website=NBA.com|date=8 February 2024|access-date=8 February 2024}}{{cite news|first=Tim|last=Bontemps|title=Hornets trade Gordon Hayward to Thunder|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39484509/hornets-trade-gordon-hayward-thunder-sources-say|website=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}} On 6 July, he was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Davis Bertans, Bryce McGowens and Aleksej Pokusevski|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-davis-bertans-bryce-mcgowens-and-aleksej-pokusevski|website=NBA.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=14 July 2024}} ===Dubai Basketball (2024–present)=== On 9 September 2024, Bertāns signed with the newly created [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[United Arab Emirates]] in the [[ABA League]].{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Davis Bertans Signs With Dubai BC|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/davis-bertans-signs-with-dubai-bc.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=10 September 2024|access-date=10 September 2024}} Over 32 games, he averaged 12.2 points and 3.2 rebounds on 47.2% shooting from the field. Dubai finished the season with loss in the [[2024–25_ABA_League_First_Division#Semifinals|semifinals]] series to Partizan Belgrade. ==National team career== Bertāns represented [[Latvia men's national basketball team|Latvia]] at [[EuroBasket 2011]], averaging 5.6 points and 2 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket2011.com/en/cid_4,w7QjPeH-M,ty138LH2l3.pageID_ZOGN4LOnIfs45jhTkYV6v0.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2011.roundID_7526.teamID_2134.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120525165019/http://www.eurobasket2011.com/en/cid_4,w7QjPeH-M,ty138LH2l3.pageID_ZOGN4LOnIfs45jhTkYV6v0.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2011.roundID_7526.teamID_2134.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=25 May 2012 |title=Latvia Roster |publisher=FIBA Europe |access-date=1 September 2011 }} He returned for [[EuroBasket 2017]], now in a more prominent role, averaging 14 points, 3 rebounds and 2 assists per game.{{cite web|title=Davis BERTANS's profile|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/Davis-Bertans|website=FIBA EuroBasket 2017|access-date=13 September 2017}} ==Personal life== Bertāns' older brother, [[Dairis Bertāns|Dairis]], is also a professional basketball player; he formerly played for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. Their father, [[Dainis Bertāns|Dainis]], was a professional basketball player and is currently a youth coach. Their mother is a sports teacher and a former high-level rower. During his childhood, Bertāns was raised in Latvia's northernmost town, [[Rūjiena]], until his parents moved to [[Rīga]], Latvia's capital. Bertāns is fluent in the [[Serbian language]].{{cite web|title=Davis Bertans za Telegraf pred duel sa Srbijom #EuroBasket2017|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YZeDTt0a7II|via=YouTube|access-date=7 September 2017}} Due to a childhood wood-cutting accident, Bertāns is missing part of the ring finger on his right hand.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/article/Spurs-Bertans-ignores-childhood-issue-that-10894354.php|title=Spurs' Bertans ignores childhood issue that cost him part of finger|first=Melissa|last=Rohlin|date=30 January 2017|website=mySA}} Bertāns is a former vegan who currently eats a dairy-free [[pescatarian]] diet;{{Cite news|date=16 January 2020|author=Buckner, Candace|title=An NBA player went pescatarian and became one of the league's best shooters|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/01/16/davis-bertans-wizards-diet-pescatarian-vegan/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20200903220601/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/01/16/davis-bertans-wizards-diet-pescatarian-vegan/|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 September 2020|access-date=3 September 2020|newspaper=The Washington Post}} having difficulty with finding good vegan food when traveling with his team influenced Bertāns' decision to change his diet.{{Cite web |last=Albert |first=Darryn |date=2020-01-17 |title=Davis Bertans credits pescatarian diet for helping him become top sharpshooter |url=https://larrybrownsports.com/basketball/davis-bertans-credits-pescatarian-diet-become-top-sharpshooter/533751 |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=Larry Brown Sports |language=en}} ==Career
